This article compares the distribution of the [[cha2ds2-vasc|CHA2DS2-VASc]] score among prevalent patients with [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]] across [[danmark|Denmark]] and its five administrative regions. The CHA2DS2-VASc score is a clinical tool used to estimate stroke risk, and tracking its distribution helps healthcare systems understand the baseline risk profile of their atrial fibrillation populations.

Across both the 2023 and 2024 reporting periods, [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] consistently recorded the highest average stroke risk, while [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] recorded the lowest [^src1] [^src2]. In 2023, the national mean score was 1.47 among 134,810 patients, with Region Sjælland leading at 1.54 and Region Hovedstaden trailing at 1.42 [^src1]. By 2024, the national mean had risen to 1.51 across 136,420 patients, with Region Sjælland again at the top (1.57) and Region Hovedstaden at the bottom (1.46) [^src2]. [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]], [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]], and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] consistently occupied the middle tiers in both years [^src1] [^src2].

Analyzing the trends between the two periods reveals a uniform, slight upward shift in mean CHA2DS2-VASc scores across the entire country. Every single region experienced an increase in its average score, ranging from a 0.03 increase in Region Syddanmark (1.52 to 1.56) to a 0.05 increase in Region Midtjylland (1.44 to 1.49) and Region Hovedstaden (1.42 to 1.46) [^src1] [^src2]. Despite this upward drift in the averages, the core distribution metrics remained entirely flat: the median score stayed at 1.00, the minimum at 0.00, and the maximum at 6.00 across all regions and nationally in both years [^src1] [^src2]. Standard deviations also showed remarkable stability, hovering between 1.06 and 1.11, indicating that while the average risk profile is slightly increasing, the spread and shape of the risk distribution remain consistent without any statistical outliers breaking the regional patterns [^src1] [^src2].
